exposure: pregnant women with ICP and fatty liver
ICP only vs. ICP with fatty liver
cohort: 43 pregnant women diagnosed with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP)
finding: While women with ICP and fatty liver had higher bile acid levels, there were no significant differences in maternal and neonatal outcomes, including mode of delivery, gestational age, maternal complications, NICU admissions, and low birth weight with asphyxia, between the two groups.
mod_finding: 51.85% of women with ICP and fatty liver underwent lower segment cesarean section (LSCS), while 43.75% with ICP without FL underwent LSCS.
